candidate.title: viscRNA-seq
candidate.scope: The central Illumina row labelled viscRNA-seq (virus-inclusive single-cell RNA sequencing), interpreted as the modified SMART-Seq2 implementation in Zanini et al., eLife 7:e32942. This row follows per-cell host and viral RNA co-capture through sequencing-ready cDNA. Modified SMART-Seq2 is an embedded component, not a separate alternative target. The partially visible SINC-Seq row above, UMI Method row below, and right-hand chemical illustration are neighboring poster content without a drawn connection to this workflow and are outside scope. The left cell-to-host/viral-RNA inset explains the biological targets rather than a second processing route. The primary paper supplies mechanistic clarifications and the cell-index interface; its unshown screening and experimental operations are not added to the diagram graph.

operations.label: FACS sort into well plates
operations.description: Distribute cells from the infected-cell population into separate wells, giving a well containing a single intact cell.
operations.mechanism: Fluorescence-activated cell sorting into 384-well plates, as stated in the row caption and primary paper.
operations.information_effect: Physical isolation associates the host and viral material subsequently recovered from each well with one cell. Sorting is not itself a measurement of the intracellular viral RNA amount.

operations.label: Capture RNA
operations.description: Engage host polyadenylated mRNA with poly-T oligonucleotides and viral RNA with virus-specific oligonucleotides in the same single-cell preparation. The output contains the two primer-accessed RNA targets for reverse transcription.
operations.mechanism: Oligo-dT recognizes host poly(A) RNA; the virus-specific DNA primer is reverse complementary to positive-strand viral RNA. The paper resolves the caption’s Viral DNA wording as viral RNA substrate. The two capture strategies are co-processing in one well, not two independent libraries.
operations.information_effect: Adds access to non-polyadenylated viral RNA alongside host mRNA. Viral inclusion depends on the supplied virus-specific primer; this does not establish universal capture of all viruses or all RNA species.

operations.label: RT and template-switching
operations.description: Convert both primer-accessed RNA populations into cDNA and extend the RT products by template switching within the Modified SMART-Seq2 component.
operations.mechanism: Uses a 5-prime-blocked template-switching oligonucleotide to reduce TSO concatemer artifacts; the primary paper specifies a biotinylated blocked TSO. No affinity capture using that biotin is depicted or reported here.
operations.information_effect: Transfers host and viral RNA sequence representation into DNA in the same cell-associated preparation. The modification reduces artifact products; it does not claim complete elimination.

method_scopes.rationale: The card title and central-row title identify one target. The paper explicitly describes viscRNA-Seq as adapted Smart-seq2 with host oligo-dT capture, a virus-specific primer and blocked TSO, matching the depicted modified SMART-Seq2 component. All five local operations belong to this row. The paper’s dengue and Zika applications instantiate this primer-specific architecture; they are not separately drawn alternative workflows. This scope does not assert identical capture for all possible RNA viruses.

corrections.diagram_observation: The capture block labels the red substrate Viral RNA, and the left inset also labels Viral RNA, but the explanatory caption below says Viral DNA captured by virus-specific oligos.
corrections.primary_statement: The primary paper states that the lysis buffer contains a DNA oligo reverse complementary to positive-strand viral RNA. Thus the captured biological substrate is viral RNA; DNA describes the capture oligonucleotide and downstream cDNA, not the starting viral analyte. op_capture and s_captured_rna are authored using this paper-supported interpretation while retaining the source caption discrepancy here.
